title: ChatGPT Is Still Not Good Enough at Giving Care-Seeking Advice, or Is It?

model.params_source: assumed (paper silent; calls went through OpenRouter with unstated parameters, and the ten-trial variability design suggests default sampling, see open_points)

task.subset_rule: all: 45 vignettes x 10 trials, each trial in a fresh context (the ten trials are the paper's repeats, so seeds = 1)
task.approximation: vignette texts and physician gold standards taken from the cited source publications; direct OpenAI API instead of OpenRouter; the two-model NLP classification plus manual adjudication of the free-text advice is replaced by a fixed classifier

items.source: 45 validated case vignettes from Kopka et al. 2024, Sci Rep 14:30614 (DOI 10.1038/s41598-024-83844-z, RepVig framework; supplementary material) and Kopka & Feufel 2024, Front Digit Health 6 (DOI 10.3389/fdgth.2024.1411924; supplementary material)
items.config_or_split: the 45-vignette set (2 emergency, 30 non-emergency, 13 self-care cases)
items.license: unknown (open-access articles; supplementary terms not checked)

prompt.user_template: Please give a triage classification for the following vignette. The criteria for triage classifications are presented below: Emergency: Call 911 or go directly to the emergency room; Non-Emergency: Try to see a doctor, but the symptoms do not require immediate attention at an emergency room. For example, you can see a doctor in the next week. Self-care: Let the health issue get better on its own and review the situation in a few days again. {case_vignette}
prompt.source_location: Methods, Outcome Evaluation paragraph (prompt quoted verbatim)

output.parse: free text mapped to label from set [emergency, non-emergency, self-care]
output.postprocess: rule: match the first explicit urgency term (Emergency / Non-Emergency / Self-care, case-insensitive) in the reply; ambiguous replies go to the zero-shot classifier named in metric.judge; compare with the gold standard

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: proportion of correctly classified cases across all 450 trials (45 vignettes x 10 trials)
metric.judge: llm:gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 (zero-shot classification of the advice into the three urgency levels; the classifier prompt is not printed and must be written)
metric.original_location: Results text: 44% of cases solved correctly (196/450); Figure 1

open_points: items not in the paper: the 45 vignettes and physician gold standards must be taken by a human from the Kopka et al. 2024 Sci Rep supplementary / Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.12805048 (the RepVig study data; the Zenodo API and record page answer 403 to scripted access) and from the Kopka & Feufel 2024 Front Digit Health supplementary, and the 45-case set (2 emergency / 30 non-emergency / 13 self-care) confirmed
decoding: the paper ran ten trials to measure variability, which implies default sampling (temperature 1.0) rather than 0; choose before running

the zero-shot classifier prompt used to map free-text advice to an urgency level is not printed; write one or rely on the rule-based mapping (hook parse), which the paper's manual adjudication would not have needed
notes: Cheap (~$0.0005 per call). Bootstrap over vignettes (45) rather than trials would be the honest unit for a CI; the paper reports the 450-trial proportion. || [hooks_3 pass 2026-09-07] no hook: the item source needs a human download and set confirmation; once a 45-row CSV (vignette, gold) is staged, the runner's 'label from set' parse and accuracy suffice.
